::: {#case .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-case">
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">1 · The puzzle</p><p>Reactor steam can either drive the <span class="lx-term" data-term="turbine">turbine</span> or feed an <span class="lx-term" data-term="absorption-chiller">absorption chiller</span> that makes chilled water.</p><p>Steam sent to the absorption chiller is steam the low-pressure turbine does not convert.</p><p class="lx-hint">So is the cooling free?</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">2 · The question in one sentence</p><p class="lx-case-q">Where should an hourly <span class="lx-term" data-term="cogeneration">cogeneration</span> study draw its <span class="lx-term" data-term="system-boundary">boundary</span>: which plant streams, which loads and which alternatives must it include to price the steam sent to cooling?</p><p class="lx-hint">The case's method question.</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">3 · Scale and boundary</p><dl class="lx-ideas cf5-bnd"><dt>Inside</dt><dd data-e14="E14.4"><ul><li>one plant with high- and low-pressure turbines,</li><li>one large load that needs power and cooling,</li><li>an absorption chiller and an electric chiller,</li><li>and power bought from and sold to the grid,</li></ul><p>every hour of a year (8,760 hours).</p></dd><dt>Left out</dt><dd data-e14="E14.6"><ul><li><span class="lx-term" data-term="demand-charge">demand charges</span> and <span class="lx-term" data-term="ancillary-services">ancillary-service</span> revenues;</li><li>reliability compared on a common basis across options;</li><li><span class="lx-term" data-term="marginal-emission-factor">marginal emission factors</span>, because emissions are counted at hourly averages;</li><li>other load profiles and sites;</li><li>the choice of plant size, because the plant is one fixed unit.</li></ul></dd></dl><p>The plant produces much more power than the load uses, so it is partly a <span class="lx-term" data-term="merchant-generator">merchant generator</span> that sells power to the grid.</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">4 · Decisions, goal and rules, in words</p><dl class="lx-ideas"><dt>Decisions</dt><dd data-e14="E14.7"><p>in every hour,</p><ul><li>the reactor's output,</li><li>the steam extracted at the <span class="lx-term" data-term="turbine-crossover">turbine crossover</span>,</li><li>how the absorption and electric chillers share the cooling,</li><li>and the power bought from or sold to the grid.</li></ul></dd><dt>Goal</dt><dd data-e14="E14.8"><p>the lowest annualized cost of meeting the load's power and cooling, counting what the power sold to the grid earns.</p></dd><dt>Rules</dt><dd data-e14="E14.9"><ul><li>the load's power and cooling are met in every hour;</li><li>every unit of steam sent to the chiller lowers turbine output;</li><li>the absorption chiller has no steam during <span class="lx-term" data-term="refuelling-outage">refueling</span>.</li></ul></dd></dl></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">5 · Data and method</p><ul><li>The value of steam cooling depends on hourly physics: <span class="lx-term" data-term="wet-bulb-temperature">wet-bulb</span> derating, <span class="lx-term" data-term="crystallization">crystallization</span> risk, <span class="lx-term" data-term="part-load-efficiency">part-load</span> chiller efficiency and the turbine work lost to extraction.</li><li>A <span class="lx-term" data-term="mixed-integer-program">mixed-integer linear program</span> <span class="lx-term" data-term="co-optimize">co-optimizes</span>, for every hour of a year, reactor output, steam extraction at the turbine crossover, absorption and electric cooling, and grid exchange.</li><li>The plant, with and without steam cooling, is compared with grid supply and an on-site gas <span class="lx-term" data-term="combined-cycle">combined cycle</span>, all evaluated on the same hourly basis.</li></ul>
<details class="lx-deeper cf5-more"><summary><span class="k">Detail</span>How the hourly physics is modeled</summary><div class="lx-deeper-body"><ul><li>Absorption performance follows hourly wet-bulb temperature with a crystallization cutoff;</li><li>the electric chiller's part-load curve uses <span class="lx-term" data-term="special-ordered-set">SOS2</span> constraints;</li><li>extraction carries a <span class="lx-term" data-term="willans-line">Willans-line</span> penalty from a <span class="lx-term" data-term="heat-balance">steam-table heat balance</span>.</li></ul></div></details>
<details class="lx-deeper cf5-more"><summary><span class="k">Detail</span>Two design choices</summary><div class="lx-deeper-body"><ul><li>Steam is extracted at the high- to low-pressure turbine crossover rather than from a parallel tap on main steam:<ul><li>crossover steam has already expanded through the high-pressure turbine, so it costs about half as much turbine work, and a sweep of the penalty tests this assumption.</li></ul></li><li>A full-size electric chiller stays beside the absorption chiller, and the optimizer chooses between the chillers hour by hour.</li></ul></div></details>
<details class="lx-deeper cf5-more"><summary><span class="k">Detail</span>Scenario runs and how results are reported</summary><div class="lx-deeper-body"><ul><li>Scenario runs vary the market year (2022 to 2024), the carbon price, the cost of capital, cooling efficiency, battery storage and the size of the load.</li><li>The load's size is swept with the plant fixed, and the grid connection is enlarged only for loads above the baseline size.</li><li><span class="lx-term" data-term="benchmark-margin">Margins</span> measured against grid cost are distorted across market years, because the grid cost itself falls in low-price years, so cross-year results are also reported in absolute annualized cost.</li></ul></div></details></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">6 · What came out, and where it holds</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:cogen-boundary-methods"><p>Pricing diverted steam matters: treating it as a free by-product can by itself decide the sign of a cogeneration result.</p><footer>From: Li et al. (2026), accepted paper, Energy Conversion and Management; DOI pending.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Holds when: steam sent to cooling would otherwise turn the low-pressure turbine; the study used one load profile, <span class="lx-term" data-term="ercot">ERCOT</span>'s hourly prices for 2022 to 2024, and one fixed plant.</p><p class="lx-hint">Leaves out: demand charges, ancillary-service revenues, and reliability on a common basis across options.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="cf5" data-src="../assets/learn/data/cf5-drawing-the-boundary.json">

(2026), accepted paper, Energy Conversion and Management; DOI pending</span></li></ol>

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The toy's four views, as arithmetic</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

The toy's symbols, for one hour: $C$ and every flow are average power over the hour, in MW; the other three are ratios.

- $C$: the cooling the load needs, in MW.
- $\mathit{COP}_e$: the electric chiller's MW of cooling per MW of electricity; it uses $C / \mathit{COP}_e$ MW of electricity.
- $\mathit{COP}_a$: the absorption chiller's MW of cooling per MW of steam heat; it takes $C / \mathit{COP}_a$ MW of steam heat.
- $w$: the MW of turbine electricity lost per MW of steam heat taken, a ratio; the steam costs the turbine $w\,C / \mathit{COP}_a$ MW.
- Left out: auxiliary electricity, such as the pumps and fans that both chillers need.

| View | Change from switching to steam cooling |
|---|---|
| Plant only, steam priced | $-\,w\,C / \mathit{COP}_a$ |
| Plant and load, steam priced | $C / \mathit{COP}_e - w\,C / \mathit{COP}_a$ |
| Plant only, turbine loss ignored | $0$ |
| Plant and load, turbine loss ignored | $+\,C / \mathit{COP}_e$ |

- Both views that ignore the turbine loss are incomplete; only the plant-and-load views include the electric chiller's saving.
- Only the plant-and-load view with the steam priced holds both sides of the switch.
- A model of a whole year adds what the toy leaves out: each hour's prices and weather, equipment limits, and the choice to switch at all.
- [M11](m11-tea-in-models.html) shows, for a wind and hydrogen plant, how hourly operation and lifetime costs fit in one optimization model.

## Check yourself, then try it
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="cf5-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="free" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Steam that would otherwise go to the turbine is free cooling.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. In the toy's defaults, 20 MW of cooling takes 25.0 MW of steam heat, which costs the turbine 5.0 MW of electricity: more than the electric chiller's 4.0 MW.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="line" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Drawing the line around the plant alone can make steam cooling look like a pure loss.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. The plant sees the turbine work it gives up (−5.0 MW in the toy) but not the electric chiller's 4.0 MW saved, which sits outside its line.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-card lx-case-try">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Try it yourself</p>
<p class="lx-hint">About 5 minutes, in the toy above.</p>
<p>Start each one from the defaults: press Reset (an ordinary hour, plant and load, steam priced, 0.20 MW of turbine work per MW of steam heat).</p>
<ul>
<li>Set the turbine work lost per MW of steam heat taken to 0.14 MW per MW, then to 0.30. Which views change their verdict, and which never can?</li>
<li>Switch to a hot, humid hour, then to a planned outage. What happens to the steam, and to the electric chiller?</li>
<li>Draw the line around the plant only, then around the plant and load. Which costs and savings cross the line?</li>
<li>Now ignore the turbine loss. Which view changes sign, and what did it leave out?</li>
</ul>
<!-- cf5-worked:start -->
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Worked answers, at the toy's defaults</summary><ul><li>At 0.14 MW of turbine work per MW of steam heat: plant and load, steam priced, +0.5 MW (steam cooling looks better); plant only, steam priced, −3.5 MW (steam cooling looks worse).</li><li>At 0.30 MW per MW: plant and load, steam priced, −3.5 MW; plant only, −7.5 MW; both worse.</li><li>The two views that ignore the turbine loss stay at 0.0 MW and +4.0 MW at any setting of the turbine work: they never change.</li><li>A hot, humid hour: 0.60 MW of cooling per MW of steam, so 20 MW of cooling takes 33.3 MW of steam heat and 6.7 MW of turbine work; plant and load, steam priced, −2.7 MW.</li><li>A planned outage: no steam, so the electric chiller carries all 20 MW of cooling with 4.0 MW of electricity; there is no switch to make.</li><li>Plant only: the 5.0 MW of turbine work is inside the line and the electric chiller's 4.0 MW saving is outside, so −5.0 MW. Plant and load: both are inside, so −1.0 MW.</li><li>Turbine loss ignored: plant and load goes from −1.0 MW to +4.0 MW, so the sign flips, because the 5.0 MW of turbine work is no longer counted; plant only goes from −5.0 MW to 0.0 MW.</li></ul></details>
<!-- cf5-worked:end -->
</div>
```
